doc.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003

title: Dizzy's spirit, intelligence and humor
summary: Dizzy was spiritual and brilliant, at ease with everyone, funny and one of the best bandleaders.

blocks.x: He was a pretty spiritual person?
Yeah he was into a lot of different spiritual things though. He had different spirits.
He ended up in, what was that —

The B’hai, yeah. The spiritual thing that comes from the East and things like that. But I think that he was more, Dizzy was just more of a great spirit in himself. More so than what he could really get out of religion. I guess he looked in there for some reason, but he had a great spirit himself. You go back and see this guy that came from a place in the south where he was living in a situation where racism and all of that was really rampant. And this guy just went through all of that like it was nothing. And Dizzy, see Dizzy was — in school Dizzy would skip a grade whenever he wanted to. He was that smart. So his brother that was next older than him, he skipped until he got into the class with him and then he finished school with him. He’s a brilliant guy you know. The kind of guy that could hear a language and things and just on his own figure out exactly how the theory of a language should be. He was like that. But you heard from what he played, his mind was working incredibly fast and on a very sophisticated level. And at the same time he could come right down to earth and be as down to earth — more down to earth than you can stand actually.

Well Dizzy could talk with a person from any level of the society and speak an English that was just incredible. Then he’d come right down and speak with the guys that had no education at all, and feel completely comfortable with them. It’s fantastic. I never was able to do that.
Quite a sense of humor, too.

A wonderful sense of humor. Could have been a comedian if he wanted to. But he always brought a lot of humor and a wonderful feeling to the people that work with him, and he treated the people with a lot of love — the musicians with a lot of love. He was one of the best band leaders around. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
